title: TSR: AFE Cell Voltage Measurement Accuracy

standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the record was written from the clause's concept ('hardware safety requirements'). Where the same rationale also says that no clause text was reproduced or consulted, that is a RIGHTS statement about wording, not a statement about influence: the record took the concept's shape and not its words, which is why the clause is its derivation basis. It is not a conformance claim - no clause was audited against this record and no assessment was performed.

The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('hardware requirements and architecture'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It is the reference project's hardware measurement requirement, written by this corpus. The hardware it describes is in Altium files in a separate repository this one cannot read, so the requirement's subject is not even visible here.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D hardware requirement with a ±1.5 mV accuracy figure mapped to ISO 26262 Part 5 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the hardware has a characterised and verified accuracy requirement. The ±1.5 mV is unsourced, the schematic anchor is unresolved because the .SchDoc is absent from this repository at every commit, and the clause is the source of the requirement's shape rather than a yardstick the hardware was measured against.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/driver/afe/api/afe.h:124 (AFE_StartMeasurement) for the measurement call the requirement is about, and FB2-SRC-HW-000002 - an Altium .SchDoc in the separate foxBMS2_hw repository, absent from this one, content_hash 'unresolved'. Pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the firmware obtains cell voltages through a named call, so measurement accuracy is a real subject. It supports NOTHING about ±1.5 mV, the -40°C to +85°C range or the 2.5V-4.2V span: none is derived from or checked against anything in this repository, and no datasheet is held here.

revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect corrected is legibility: this record was already marked `profile: synthetic_reference` and, for the SYRs, already says in its own limitations field that it establishes nothing about the real project - but a reader skimming `artifact_type`, `asil` and `standards_mappings` sees a safety requirement at an ASIL with an ISO 26262 clause and status `mapped`, and reads it as an allocated, conformant safety obligation of the product. It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: The AFE shall measure cell voltages with ±1.5 mV accuracy (including calibration) over -40°C to +85°C for 2.5V-4.2V range.
rationale: Required to support SOA limit detection with 1 mV threshold accuracy (FSR-002)
provenance_note: Provenance re-checked 2026-10-01 after the source-registry repair. This record's source_refs pointed at anchor(s) that named C symbols existing nowhere in the repository. Those anchors now name real, verified symbols and carry real content hashes. Origin remains synthetic, which already declared this content modelled rather than observed.
